skill.name: image-outpainting
skill.description: Extend and uncrop images with RunComfy edit models. The skill helps route aspect-ratio changes, canvas expansion, and reference-style outpainting through the RunComfy CLI.
skill.summary: Extend image canvases and change aspect ratios with RunComfy outpainting routes.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: The static backtick findings are Markdown inline code, fenced examples, or model identifiers, not executable Ruby backticks. Hardcoded URLs are visible documentation links or placeholders, and the token path is disclosed storage with restrictive permissions. The only remaining concern is expected third-party processing through RunComfy, which requires user consent for sensitive images.

remediation.suggestion: Ask for user consent before sending prompts, source image URLs, or reference images to RunComfy services.
Keep install and login steps opt-in, and prefer an existing RunComfy CLI installation when available.
Keep the documented 0600 token path and add token rotation guidance for shared machines.

content.value_statement: Changing aspect ratios can damage composition or erase important subject details. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to route outpainting requests through RunComfy edit models.
actual_capabilities: Selects RunComfy edit routes for simple outpainting, reference-style matching, and brand-locked continuations.
Provides prompt patterns for aspect-ratio changes, portrait uncropping, product shots, and hero images.
Shows RunComfy CLI usage with inputs, output directories, and model identifiers.
Explains when to use Nano Banana 2 Edit, GPT Image 2 Edit, FLUX Kontext Pro, or brand edit endpoints.
Documents exit codes, endpoint allowlists, generated file limits, and token storage behavior.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy login before model calls can run.
Sends prompts and image references to RunComfy services for processing.
Does not provide mask-driven local inpainting or video outpainting workflows.
Dedicated ComfyUI workflows may be needed for pixel-precise seam control.

use_cases.title: Create social media crops
use_cases.description: Convert square or landscape images into vertical posts while preserving the main subject and extending the background.

use_cases.title: Prepare product catalog images
use_cases.description: Uncrop product shots and add matching surroundings for banners, marketplace listings, or campaign layouts.

use_cases.title: Restore cropped archive photos
use_cases.description: Use reference images and preservation prompts to extend old photographs without changing the visible original area.

prompt_templates.title: Uncrop a portrait
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple canvas extension.
prompt_templates.prompt: Outpaint this portrait downward to show more of the upper body. Match the clothing, lighting, and background. Keep the face unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Make a wide banner
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a specific aspect ratio.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this square image to 16:9. Add matching environment on both sides and preserve the central subject exactly.

prompt_templates.title: Match a reference style
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using another image as style guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the original image and this reference image to outpaint a wider scene. Match the reference lighting and keep the original subject intact.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a weak outpaint
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multi-step request when seams or lighting do not match.
prompt_templates.prompt: The last outpaint has visible seams. Choose a better RunComfy route, preserve the original area, and extend only 30 percent per pass.

output_examples.input: A square portrait needs to become a wide website hero image.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects Nano Banana 2 Edit, asks for a 16:9 canvas, preserves the face, and saves the wider result.

output_examples.input: A product photo is cropped too tightly for a catalog banner.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates an outpainting prompt that continues the surface, lighting, and shadow direction around the product.

output_examples.input: An archive photo needs more surrounding context and a period reference is available.
output_examples.output: The assistant routes to a reference-aware edit model and keeps the original visible area unchanged.

best_practices: Lead prompts with the required canvas change and target aspect ratio.
Describe lighting, camera distance, background texture, and color continuity.
Use explicit preservation language for faces, products, logos, and other important details.
anti_patterns: Do not send private or licensed images to RunComfy without user permission.
Do not ask for large single-pass extensions when several smaller passes would preserve quality.
Do not use this skill for mask-based inpainting or video canvas expansion.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps extend an image canvas, uncrop a photo, or change aspect ratio through RunComfy edit models.

faq.question: Which model does it use by default?
faq.answer: It prefers Nano Banana 2 Edit for prompt-shaped outpainting and switches routes when references or preservation needs require it.

faq.question: Can it match another image style?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends GPT Image 2 Edit when a reference image should guide the extended area.

faq.question: Does it edit local pixels without sending data?
faq.answer: No. It uses RunComfy services, so prompts and image references are processed by RunComfy.

faq.question: Can it fix visible seams?
faq.answer: It can suggest a better route or smaller extension passes. Dedicated ComfyUI workflows may be needed for fine seam control.

faq.question: Does it support video outpainting?
faq.answer: No. The skill is for still images and points users to a separate video outpainting skill.
